pages.title: ON Semiconductor Climbs After Replacing Its $7 Billion Stock Bid With a $5.7 Billion Cash Synaptics Offer
pages.text:
NEW YORK — ON Semiconductor shares rose Friday after the chipmaker replaced an all-stock agreement to buy Synaptics with a smaller all-cash bid, a cut in headline price that investors treated as a better deal for the buyer.
The stock traded at $84.94, up $4.85, or 6.06 percent, in morning dealings. Other screens showed the shares as high as about $86, up roughly 8 percent. Synaptics jumped more sharply, about 14 percent, to around $121, just under the new offer price.
Under the amended merger agreement, ON Semiconductor will pay $123 in cash for each Synaptics share, a transaction valued at about $5.7 billion. The June deal had been all stock and had valued Synaptics at about $7 billion. The revision followed an unsolicited competing proposal for Synaptics from a third party. The Synaptics board unanimously backed the amended transaction.
"As was the case when we initially announced the acquisition, Synaptics addresses an important aspect of our strategic direction, and we believe the revised merger agreement represents a more financially attractive transaction for our shareholders," ON Semiconductor Chief Executive Hassane El-Khoury said in a statement. He also said the all-cash structure "delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration."
The company said it expects the deal to be immediately accretive to adjusted earnings per share at closing. Funding is to come from cash on hand and committed debt financing, with no closing condition tied to that financing. Reports put committed financing near $2.45 billion. Completion is targeted for mid-2027, subject to Synaptics shareholder approval and customary regulatory clearances.

The arithmetic explains the split reaction. Synaptics holders get a fixed cash price instead of ON shares whose value had fallen. ON Semiconductor stock is down about a third from its midsummer highs, which had shrunk the implied value of the original stock offer and raised doubt that the June terms would hold. Paying cash at $5.7 billion instead of issuing stock at a $7 billion valuation removes dilution and lowers the consideration, which is why the buyer's shares rose on a smaller bid.
Synaptics is an Internet-of-things and interface company whose sensing chips sit at the edge of devices rather than in the data-center processors that have led the semiconductor rally. Management has said it expects fiscal 2026 core IoT revenue to grow more than 40 percent, to more than $385 million, on Edge AI and physical-AI design wins. For ON Semiconductor, the point of the deal is to add that sensing and interface layer to a portfolio built on power devices, including silicon carbide, sold into cars, factories and, increasingly, artificial-intelligence power systems.
That strategy was the subject of the company's investor day. El-Khoury has said that as AI, electrification and automation expand, power density "has emerged as one of the key engineering challenges that will define the next decade," and that the ability to supply power, sense the environment and support decisions "will determine the next generation of intelligent devices." The company has projected a total effective market across automotive, industrial, AI data centers and next-generation uses of $213 billion by 2030. It has also said the AI data-center piece of its business is set to more than double in 2026 and double again in 2027.
Friday's move sits on top of an already strong week. ON Semiconductor closed Thursday at $80.08, up 4.18 percent, before the cash-deal details fully reset the tape. The Friday gain is the market pricing the revised merger, not a second earnings surprise.
Risks remain the ordinary ones in a cash acquisition announced after a competing approach. A higher bid from the unnamed third party could reopen the price. Regulators still have to clear a combination of power semiconductors and edge-sensing chips. Debt taken on to fund $123 a share will sit on a balance sheet that investors had not been asked to lever for this deal in June. And "immediately accretive" is an adjusted figure that excludes the costs of getting there.
For Synaptics holders, the trade is simpler. A stock deal whose value drifted with ON's share price has become a cash bid within a few dollars of where the stock now trades. The board's unanimous support and the premium to the undisturbed price are why SYNA outperformed the buyer on the day.
For ON Semiconductor holders, the gain is a vote that $5.7 billion in cash is preferable to $7 billion in stock for a business meant to extend the company from power into sensing. El-Khoury's case is that the strategic fit has not changed and the terms have improved. The share price on Friday said the market agreed, at least for a morning.

A revised takeover agreement is lifting both the buyer and the target in a chip deal that just got simpler. On Semiconductor (NASDAQ:ON | ON Price Prediction) stock is at $86.64, up 8% in morning trading. This follows the company replacing its $7 billion all-stock agreement to buy Synaptics (NASDAQ:SYNA) with a $5.7 billion all-cash bid.
Synaptics stock is up 14% to $121.32, a larger climb tied to a fixed cash price replacing a floating share exchange.
The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) is up 3% to $590.75, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) trades at $752.16, up 1.36%. That gap shows how much of the move traces to the deal itself.
Under an amended merger agreement, On Semiconductor will pay $123 in cash for each Synaptics share, replacing the all-stock structure. The amendment followed an unsolicited competing proposal for Synaptics from a third party.
On Semiconductor now expects the transaction to be immediately accretive to adjusted earnings per share upon closing. CEO Hassane El-Khoury stated: “The all-cash transaction delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration.” Funding comes from cash on hand and committed debt financing, with no closing condition tied to that financing.
Dilution Fades for On Semiconductor, Certainty Arrives for Synaptics
For On Semiconductor shareholders, the core change is the removal of dilution. Paying cash leaves the share count untouched, protecting buyback work that included $332 million of repurchases in Q2 2026.
A fixed cash price gives Synaptics investors certainty, and the Synaptics board unanimously backed the amended transaction.
Synaptics also brings growth. Its management expects fiscal 2026 Core Internet of Things (IoT) revenue to grow more than 40% to over $385 million, driven by Edge AI and Physical AI design wins. On Semiconductor management stated on the August 3 earnings call that Synaptics’ “market-leading connected compute capabilities” complement On Semiconductor’s “strength in power, sensing, and control.”
The trade-off is debt. Cash and short-term investments totaled $3.9 billion at the end of Q2, with total liquidity of $5.4 billion. Quarterly free cash flow reached $425 million, a support for paying down new borrowing.
The U.S. Federal Trade Commission has approved the deal, but other jurisdictions are still reviewing it, and Synaptics shareholders must vote. On August 3, On Semiconductor expected the transaction to close in mid-2027.
Investors can watch for the Synaptics stockholder vote and remaining reviews in other jurisdictions before On Semiconductor closes the purchase, as details on the committed debt financing cost could shape how the market judges On Semiconductor’s balance sheet.
Immediate accretion and an AI data center business where management expects revenue to more than double in 2026 support the optimistic view (we covered seven suppliers riding that same AI infrastructure expansion, from power to cooling, in a free report). Risks center on new leverage and integrating Synaptics.
Synaptics shareholders now face an outcome fixed at the $123 cash price. Traders may watch whether On Semiconductor stock holds its gains as borrowing terms become clearer.

The stock of intelligent power and sensing chip company ON Semiconductor (ON +0.44%) has had a wild ride in 2026. It delivered an exceptional performance, driven by a combination of soaring demand from its fast-growing artificial intelligence (AI) data center market and a cyclical recovery in its core automotive and industrial end markets.
However, the announcement of an agreement to acquire AI edge solutions company Synaptics (SYNA -0.28%) led to a crash in the share price, and the recent investor day presentation didn't reverse it. What's going on and why isn't the market warming to the company's strategic shift?
A slew of Wall Street analysts lowered their price targets for the stock after the investor day presentation, in which management outlined plans to target a market valued at $213 billion. However, as ever, it's hard to discern if the cuts were in response to the presentation or a lowering of price targets now that the market has corrected the stock so sharply.

Whatever the case, the market appears to still be treating ON Semiconductor in terms of where it's come from rather than where it's going. In other words, a chip company is exposed to highly cyclical end markets. The sharp rise in the price earlier in the year reflects the cyclical recovery in its end markets, as well as strong growth in its AI data center end market (reported under "other") from which management expects $500 million in revenue this year, with expectations for $1 billion in 2027 and $2.5 billion in 2030.
However, the crash in the share price since the Synaptics announcement indicates the market is not happy with the company's strategic shift from being a component supplier to an integrated technology platform provider.

Management aims to capture more value from its end markets by providing power system architectures that are a naturally evolving necessity for physical AI solutions requiring ever-greater power density. These power architectures will, in the words of CEO Hassane El-Khoury during the investor day, link "to a connected compute platform that is at the center," which is where Synaptics solutions will come in and help expand its addressable market from $213 billion to $243 billion.
Clearly, the market is ignoring the strategic shift, or rather, doesn't believe in it.

That argument is supported when you look at what management guided toward in the investor day presentation regarding revenue growth (see the table below). Moreover, management forecasts its gross margin will expand from 40.3% in 2026 to 53% in 2030, with gross profit growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 22% and operating income at a 30% CAGR over the period.
To apply these metrics to valuations, management expects to generate $3.5 billion in free cash flow (FCF) in 2030. Very conservatively, the business at 20 times FCF would imply a stock price of $179, up from $70 now, with a potential annual return of 26%. And none of these metrics include any assumptions from Synaptics, since the acquisition hasn't been completed yet.

Management's core argument that the increasing need for power density is creating a significant opportunity for ON Semiconductor to capture more value by offering an integrated power architecture is sound. That applies whether it's data centers needing more power for AI racks, EVs needing higher power density for ultra-fast charging, or a range of physical AI products, such as humanoid robots.
However, the market appears worried, either about the company's ability to execute or the traditional cyclicality of its end markets over the near term. The latter is a definite consideration, as seen in the volatility of sales in the first chart. Still, it's incredibly difficult to predict these trends, and the underlying growth driver -- the secular increase in the demand for power density -- is strong.
On that basis, ON Semiconductor remains a highly attractive stock for AI-focused investors with a long-term view.

ON Semiconductor (ON) Switches to $5.7B All-Cash Synaptics Acquisition, Stock Jumps 6%
By Trader EdgeOctober 2, 2026No Comments3 Mins Read
ON Semiconductor restructured its Synaptics acquisition into an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $5.7 billion, reduced from the initial $7 billion stock-based proposal.
Synaptics shareholders will receive $123 cash per share rather than the previously agreed 1.350 ON shares from the June announcement.
ON stock surged approximately 6% during premarket hours, while Synaptics shares climbed roughly 14%.
The restructured agreement eliminates shareholder dilution concerns for ON investors and promises immediate accretion to non-GAAP earnings.
Completion of the transaction requires Synaptics shareholder approval and regulatory clearances, with an expected closing date in mid-2027.
Shares of ON Semiconductor rallied approximately 6% in Friday’s premarket session following the company’s announcement of a restructured takeover agreement with Synaptics. The stock had ended Thursday’s session at $80.08.
Synaptics shares posted even stronger gains, climbing approximately 14% on the announcement. Both semiconductor companies specialize in chip technologies for automotive, industrial, and Internet of Things applications.
The initial agreement, announced in June, proposed an all-stock merger structure. Under those terms, Synaptics shareholders would have exchanged each share for 1.350 ON Semiconductor shares, establishing a transaction value near $7 billion.
The revised agreement converts the transaction to an all-cash purchase. Synaptics shareholders will now receive $123 in cash per share, reducing the total transaction value to approximately $5.7 billion.
The price reduction followed an unsolicited competing proposal for Synaptics from an unnamed third party. Rather than triggering a competitive bidding situation that elevated the acquisition price, the development prompted both parties to negotiate modified terms more favorable to each company.
ON shareholders sidestep the equity dilution that would have resulted from issuing new shares under the original agreement. This change eliminates a significant concern that had pressured the stock since the June announcement.
The company indicates the restructured transaction will immediately enhance its non-GAAP earnings per share. This represents a meaningful improvement from the original structure, which wasn’t projected to be immediately accretive to earnings.
ON had previously identified $200 million in annual cost synergies from the combination. The company now anticipates additional opportunities, including potential revenue synergies and internalizing certain Synaptics manufacturing operations.
The transaction will be funded through a combination of existing cash reserves and debt financing arranged by Morgan Stanley. The absence of a financing contingency for closing eliminates another potential risk factor.
Synaptics CEO Rahul Patel characterized the cash structure as delivering certainty to investors. “We are providing value certainty at a premium as compared to current value,” he said.
The revised terms present a clear tradeoff. Synaptics shareholders forfeit potential participation in the merged entity’s future performance, receiving instead a guaranteed cash payment.
Robert W. Baird analyst Tristan Gerra maintained a Hold rating on ON stock following the announcement, keeping his $108 price target. The broader Wall Street consensus rates ON a Moderate Buy, while Synaptics carries a Hold rating.
Market timing also worked in the company’s favor. Micron’s impressive earnings results released the previous evening had already elevated semiconductor stocks broadly, providing additional momentum for ON’s announcement heading into Friday’s opening.
Treasury yields retreated from recent peaks that same morning, relieving some pressure on growth-oriented technology stocks.
The acquisition still requires approval from Synaptics shareholders alongside regulatory clearances. While the FTC has already granted approval, reviews in additional jurisdictions remain pending.
The companies are targeting a mid-2027 closing timeline. Between now and then, both stocks will likely respond to progress updates on the approval process.

ON Semiconductor's revised Synaptics deal improves earnings outlook, says BofA
ON Semiconductor’s revised $5.7 billion acquisition of Synaptics could deliver a bigger earnings boost than originally expected while eliminating the share dilution that had weighed on the deal, Bank of America said.
Following an unsolicited competing proposal, the companies amended their June 25 agreement to replace the all-stock transaction with a $123-per-share cash offer.
The deal's aggregate value falls to approximately $5.7 billion from $7 billion, eliminating roughly 59 million additional shares and the previously contemplated 12% to 13% dilution.
With ON Semiconductor shares down 32% since the deal's announcement, Bank of America wrote that revised terms could improve investor reception by removing dilution while preserving the strategic rationale.
ON Semiconductor would fund the deal with cash on hand and approximately $2.5 billion in term loan debt, with no financing condition.
Even with that borrowing, the broker estimates the transaction could increase earnings per share by approximately 11% in calendar 2027 and 15% in calendar 2028.
Its combined-company EPS estimates are $5 and $6.88, respectively, compared with standalone forecasts of $4.51 and $5.99.
Those projected gains reflect an estimated 4% dilution and 2% accretion under the original structure, primarily from eliminating additional shares.
The revised model includes cost synergies of $90 million and $175 million, respectively, partly offset by a roughly $150 million annual financial-income headwind from cash-and-debt funding.
The estimates exclude revenue synergies and potential outsourcing benefits beyond the previously announced $200 million annual cost-synergy target, and management expects to outsource some SYNA production after the first 18 months following closing.
The acquisition would also broaden ON Semiconductor's portfolio, with Bank of America highlighting SYNA's edge computing, connectivity, software, and human-machine interfaces alongside existing power and sensing capabilities.
The broker expects the combination to support more integrated solutions across industrial markets, robotics, autonomous driving, and augmented and virtual reality.
It estimates the acquisition would expand ON Semiconductor's calendar 2030 addressable market by approximately $30 billion to $243 billion.
Bank of America still expects completion by mid-2027, with FTC approval received and other regulatory reviews ongoing.

Synaptics Inc. (NASDAQ:SYNA) extended its winning streak to a fourth straight session on Friday, surging 14.08 percent on Friday to finish at $121.10 apiece, following ON Semiconductor's decision to switch its acquisition of the former to an all-cash transaction.
Week on week, the stock climbed 17.9 percent.
In an update later Thursday, ON Semiconductor said it is now planning to acquire Synaptics Inc. (NASDAQ:SYNA) for $123 per share, down from its original offer of 1.350 ON Semi shares for every SYNA stock held by its shareholders.
Although downsized to $5.7 billion from the original $7 billion, SYNA investors gobbled up its stock to take advantage of the nearly 16 percent premium over its closing price on Thursday.
"By transitioning to an all-cash structure, we are providing value certainty at a meaningful premium as compared to current value. We are confident this path is the right choice for our shareholders," Synaptics Inc. (NASDAQ:SYNA) President and CEO Rahul Patel said.
"Our Board has been singularly focused on delivering the best outcome for our shareholders, and today's amended agreement reflects that commitment," he noted.
ON Semiconductor is set to finance the transaction through a combination of cash on hand and committed financing from Morgan Stanley.
The transaction is expected to close in the middle of next year, subject to approval of Synaptics Inc. (NASDAQ:SYNA) shareholders, while its board of directors will join ON Semiconductor's board.
The acquisition followed Synaptics Inc.'s (NASDAQ:SYNA) soaring losses in both the fourth quarter and full fiscal year 2026.
In the last quarter ending June 27, the company said that net losses widened by 9,419 percent to $447.4 million from only $4.7 million in the same period last year, dragged by a $425.3 million non-cash charge related to the establishment of a valuation allowance against US deferred tax assets, which is excluded from non-GAAP results.
Revenues, on the other hand, increased by 8.9 percent to $308 million from $282.8 million year-on-year.
In full fiscal year 2026, net losses soared by 927 percent to $490.8 million from $47.8 million, while revenues increased by 11 percent to $1.197 billion from $1.074 billion last year.
Despite the results, institutional investors remained optimistic about the company's long-term growth prospects, as evidenced by the increase in hedge fund holders establishing exposure, alongside their committed capital.

ON Semiconductor (NASDAQ:ON | ON Price Prediction) trades at $68.30 after a brutal summer, while the average Wall Street price target sits at $106.88. That leaves the stock roughly 56% below where analysts, on average, think it should trade.
ON is the Phoenix-based designer behind onsemi, a top supplier of intelligent power and sensing chips for cars, factories, and increasingly, AI server racks. Its EliteSiC silicon carbide and GaNEXUS gallium nitride families are pitched as the plumbing for 800-volt vehicle platforms and the next generation of hyperscaler power trees. Wall Street cares because that story sits at the intersection of two of the biggest capex cycles in tech.
Even after a brutal selloff, business metrics are improving and analysts have not wavered. One has doubled down.
A Three-Month Wipeout in a Rallying Market
Shares of ON have plunged 43.84% over the past three months, a decline steep enough to qualify as a full-blown crash. The stock started that window at $121.62 and has bled all the way down to its current level, with a 14% drop just in the last month.
The selloff came despite strong results. Q2 fiscal 2026 revenue of $1.60 billion beat estimates and rose 9.18% year over year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.74 topping the $0.7153 consensus. Shares popped more than 5% after the report. The unwind has been driven by broader concerns: high automotive exposure, China cyclicality, a rich trailing valuation, and profit-taking after a run that had ON near $134.92 on a 52-week basis. The peer group softened too, but ON fell harder and faster.
Why Susquehanna Still Sees Roughly 120% Upside
Analysts have not chased the stock lower. Coverage sits at 2 Strong Buy, 11 Buy, 16 Hold, and zero Sell ratings, and estimate revisions have skewed sharply higher, with 25 upward EPS revisions for fiscal 2026 in the trailing 30 days against just two down.
Susquehanna’s Christopher Rolland reiterated a Buy with a Street-high $150 price target, implying roughly 120% upside from $68.30. His thesis: EliteSiC capturing dominant share as EV platforms shift from 400V to 800V architectures, AI data center power scaling through smart power stages and point-of-load converters, and gross margins recovering toward 40%+.
Management backs that narrative. AI data center is now expected to more than double in 2026. CEO Hassane El-Khoury told investors, “Our growth in data center is literally from the wall to the core.” Silicon carbide revenue in data centers is guided to grow nearly 60% year over year, with content per rack jumping from $15,000 to $115,000 in an 800-volt DC architecture. Non-GAAP gross margin already expanded to 39.3%, with Q3 guidance calling for 40% to 42%.
Analog Peers Held Up While ON Broke Down
This selloff is largely a single-name story. Peers softened but held ground.
NXP Semiconductors (NASDAQ:NXPI) trades at $227.95 against a target of $311.10, roughly 36% of implied upside. NXPI is up 5.02% year to date with 6 Strong Buy, 16 Buy, 7 Hold and 1 Sell ratings, a solidly bullish tilt.
Analog Devices (NASDAQ:ADI) has been the sector standout, up 33.72% year to date at $362.65 against a $470.72 target, about 30% upside. Coverage skews aggressively bullish at 7 Strong Buy, 24 Buy, 3 Hold.
ON’s analyst-implied upside is the widest in the group. That makes ON the outlier in the group.
ON trades at $68.30 versus a consensus target of $106.88 from 30 covering analysts, implying 56% upside to the average and about 120% to Susquehanna’s $150. The forward P/E of 16 reflects the sharp fiscal 2026 earnings ramp analysts are modeling toward $3.2028 full-year EPS.
ON is up 26.13% year to date, ahead of the S&P 500‘s 11.85%, but that lead was built and lost in a violent round trip. Over three months, ON’s 43.84% drawdown stands in stark contrast to a flat-to-up broad market.
The bull case for ON here rests on the AI data center ramp and silicon carbide share gains materializing over the next few quarters. Q3 guidance already points to gross margins of 40% to 42%, book-to-bill has been above 1 for several quarters, and lead times have extended to roughly 32 weeks. Deliver on those numbers and even the consensus $106.88 becomes conservative.
The bear case centers on automotive weakness in Europe, China exposure, and the pending Synaptics acquisition integration risk are what the market is pricing in. A stalled industrial recovery or a slip in AI content per rack could keep the multiple compressed.
My lean is cautiously bullish. The analyst dispersion is wide for a reason, but the operating data is moving in the bulls’ direction, and ON’s dislocation looks larger than the fundamentals justify.

ON Semiconductor stock (ISIN US6821891035) closed at USD 66.60 on the Nasdaq on September 16, 2026, down 9.0 percent from the prior session and extending a multi-week slide for the chipmaker as investors digested fresh guidance and analyst commentary around its long-term growth strategy.
Investor Day triggers sharp single-day drop
According to an article from Ad-hoc-news.de on September 17, 2026, ON Semiconductor stock fell from an opening level around USD 74.42 to a close at USD 66.60 on September 16, 2026, erasing roughly USD 2 billion in market value and marking an unusually large daily swing for the name.
The same report cites data from Investing.com and 24/7 Wall St. showing that during the September 16, 2026 session the shares traded between an intraday high near USD 74.42 and a low around USD 66.50, underperforming broader semiconductor indices that were roughly flat to modestly higher on the day.
As Tickeron reported on September 17, 2026, the September 16 Investor Day became the biggest catalyst in the past month, with the stock dropping about 9 percent in that single session and contributing to a roughly 16 percent decline over the prior 30 days from around USD 79.42 on August 18, 2026 to USD 66.60 by the September 16, 2026 close.
Long-term targets and Q2 2026 fundamentals
At its Investor Day on September 16, 2026, ON Semiconductor outlined a long-term growth strategy focused on power solutions for AI, electrification and automation, including an updated revenue ambition for the coming decade. As described by Moomoo on September 17, 2026, the company presented its roadmap to power the next decade of innovation by addressing growing power constraints in AI data centers, electric vehicles and industrial automation.
Alongside the strategy discussion, investors have been weighing the latest quarterly figures. In Q2 2026, reported on August 3, 2026, ON Semiconductor delivered revenue of USD 1.60 billion, which was up 9.2 percent year over year from roughly USD 1.47 billion in the same quarter of 2025 and slightly ahead of the USD 1.59 billion consensus estimate according to MarketBeat.
The same MarketBeat overview notes that earnings per share for Q2 2026 came in at USD 0.74, beating the consensus forecast of USD 0.72 by USD 0.02 and improving from USD 0.53 in the comparable quarter a year earlier, while net margin stood at 10.17 percent and return on equity at 14.06 percent.
Looking ahead, ON Semiconductor has issued guidance for Q3 2026 with expected earnings per share between USD 0.81 and USD 0.93, implying sequential growth from the Q2 2026 level of USD 0.74 and underpinning analyst forecasts that, as summarized by MarketBeat, point to full-year 2026 earnings per share of about USD 3.23.
Analysts recalibrate price targets and ratings
The sharp price reaction around the Investor Day has been accompanied by an active period of analyst updates on ON Semiconductor stock. On September 17, 2026, Needham reiterated a Buy rating on the shares and maintained a price target of USD 116, according to MarketBeat.
A parallel alert from MarketBeat on September 17, 2026 indicates that Cantor Fitzgerald cut its price target on ON Semiconductor from USD 110 to USD 90 while keeping a Neutral rating, aligning its valuation with a multiple of 14 times its calendar year 2028 upside earnings per share estimate versus 17 times previously.
On the same day, MarketBeat reported that Wells Fargo reduced its price target on ON Semiconductor from USD 95 to USD 85 while maintaining an Overweight rating, citing updated assumptions on margins and sector multiples.
As a further data point, Rosenblatt Securities reaffirmed a Neutral rating with a USD 85 price objective, and MarketBeat notes that, based on its compilation of coverage, ON Semiconductor currently carries a consensus rating of Moderate Buy with an average price target of USD 93.36, providing a benchmark against the September 16, 2026 close at USD 66.60.
An analysis from Investing.com on September 17, 2026 highlights that Stifel lowered its price target on ON Semiconductor stock from USD 90 to USD 75 while maintaining a Hold rating, citing margin outlook concerns as a key factor.
The same Investing.com piece notes that Cantor Fitzgerald and Mizuho also reduced their targets, with Cantor moving from USD 110 to USD 90 and Mizuho from USD 110 to USD 95, while retaining Neutral and Outperform ratings respectively, and that Wells Fargo trimmed its forecast to USD 95 from USD 110 with an Overweight stance.
For investors, the divergence between the adjusted price targets in the USD 75 to USD 116 range and the current stock level around USD 66.60 underscores a debate about how quickly ON Semiconductor can translate its power-focused roadmap and silicon carbide content into sustained earnings growth and margin expansion.
Risks mentioned across analyst and media coverage include sensitivity to automotive and industrial demand cycles, execution on AI data center opportunities, and the possibility that higher interest rates or sector-wide valuation compression could further weigh on multiples even if fundamentals remain intact.

The recent drawdown has also pushed the shares well below commonly watched moving averages. From a medium-term perspective, Tickeron calculates that ON Semiconductor shares have fallen around 44 percent over the past quarter while remaining positive year to date, suggesting that despite the recent volatility, longer-horizon investors still see potential in the company’s positioning in power semiconductors for vehicles and data centers.

Synaptics is an Internet-of-things and interface company whose sensing chips sit at the edge of devices rather than in the data-center processors that have led the semiconductor rally. Management has said it expects fiscal 2026 core IoT revenue to grow more than 40 percent, to more than $385 million, on Edge AI and physical-AI design wins. For ON Semiconductor, the point of the deal is to add that sensing and interface layer to a portfolio built on power devices, including silicon carbide, sold into cars, factories and, increasingly, artificial-intelligence power systems.
That strategy was the subject of the company's investor day. El-Khoury has said that as AI, electrification and automation expand, power density "has emerged as one of the key engineering challenges that will define the next decade," and that the ability to supply power, sense the environment and support decisions "will determine the next generation of intelligent devices." Regulators still have to clear a combination of power semiconductors and edge-sensing chips. Debt taken on to fund $123 a share will sit on a balance sheet that investors had not been asked to lever for this deal in June. For Synaptics holders, the trade is simpler. A stock deal whose value drifted with ON's share price has become a cash bid within a few dollars of where the stock now trades. The board's unanimous support and the premium to the undisturbed price are why SYNA outperformed the buyer on the day.
For ON Semiconductor holders, the gain is a vote that $5.7 billion in cash is preferable to $7 billion in stock for a business meant to extend the company from power into sensing. El-Khoury's case is that the strategic fit has not changed and the terms have improved. The share price on Friday said the market agreed, at least for a morning.

A revised takeover agreement is lifting both the buyer and the target in a chip deal that just got simpler. On Semiconductor (NASDAQ:ON | ON Price Prediction) stock is at $86.64, up 8% in morning trading. This follows the company replacing its $7 billion all-stock agreement to buy Synaptics (NASDAQ:SYNA) with a $5.7 billion all-cash bid.
Synaptics stock is up 14% to $121.32, a larger climb tied to a fixed cash price replacing a floating share exchange.
The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) is up 3% to $590.75, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) trades at $752.16, up 1.36%. That gap shows how much of the move traces to the deal itself.
Under an amended merger agreement, On Semiconductor will pay $123 in cash for each Synaptics share, replacing the all-stock structure. The amendment followed an unsolicited competing proposal for Synaptics from a third party.
On Semiconductor now expects the transaction to be immediately accretive to adjusted earnings per share upon closing. CEO Hassane El-Khoury stated: “The all-cash transaction delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration.” Funding comes from cash on hand and committed debt financing, with no closing condition tied to that financing.
Dilution Fades for On Semiconductor, Certainty Arrives for Synaptics
For On Semiconductor shareholders, the core change is the removal of dilution. Paying cash leaves the share count untouched, protecting buyback work that included $332 million of repurchases in Q2 2026.
A fixed cash price gives Synaptics investors certainty, and the Synaptics board unanimously backed the amended transaction.
Synaptics also brings growth. Its management expects fiscal 2026 Core Internet of Things (IoT) revenue to grow more than 40% to over $385 million, driven by Edge AI and Physical AI design wins. On Semiconductor management stated on the August 3 earnings call that Synaptics’ “market-leading connected compute capabilities” complement On Semiconductor’s “strength in power, sensing, and control.”
The trade-off is debt. Cash and short-term investments totaled $3.9 billion at the end of Q2, with total liquidity of $5.4 billion. Quarterly free cash flow reached $425 million, a support for paying down new borrowing.
The U.S. Federal Trade Commission has approved the deal, but other jurisdictions are still reviewing it, and Synaptics shareholders must vote. On August 3, On Semiconductor expected the transaction to close in mid-2027.
Investors can watch for the Synaptics stockholder vote and remaining reviews in other jurisdictions before On Semiconductor closes the purchase, as details on the committed debt financing cost could shape how the market judges On Semiconductor’s balance sheet.
Immediate accretion and an AI data center business where management expects revenue to more than double in 2026 support the optimistic view (we covered seven suppliers riding that same AI infrastructure expansion, from power to cooling, in a free report). Risks center on new leverage and integrating Synaptics.
Synaptics shareholders now face an outcome fixed at the $123 cash price. Traders may watch whether On Semiconductor stock holds its gains as borrowing terms become clearer.

A slew of Wall Street analysts lowered their price targets for the stock after the investor day presentation, in which management outlined plans to target a market valued at $213 billion. Whatever the case, the market appears to still be treating ON Semiconductor in terms of where it's come from rather than where it's going. In other words, a chip company is exposed to highly cyclical end markets. The sharp rise in the price earlier in the year reflects the cyclical recovery in its end markets, as well as strong growth in its AI data center end market (reported under "other") from which management expects $500 million in revenue this year, with expectations for $1 billion in 2027 and $2.5 billion in 2030.
However, the crash in the share price since the Synaptics announcement indicates the market is not happy with the company's strategic shift from being a component supplier to an integrated technology platform provider.

Management aims to capture more value from its end markets by providing power system architectures that are a naturally evolving necessity for physical AI solutions requiring ever-greater power density. These power architectures will, in the words of CEO Hassane El-Khoury during the investor day, link "to a connected compute platform that is at the center," which is where Synaptics solutions will come in and help expand its addressable market from $213 billion to $243 billion.

To apply these metrics to valuations, management expects to generate $3.5 billion in free cash flow (FCF) in 2030. That applies whether it's data centers needing more power for AI racks, EVs needing higher power density for ultra-fast charging, or a range of physical AI products, such as humanoid robots.

The latter is a definite consideration, as seen in the volatility of sales in the first chart. Still, it's incredibly difficult to predict these trends, and the underlying growth driver -- the secular increase in the demand for power density -- is strong.
On that basis, ON Semiconductor remains a highly attractive stock for AI-focused investors with a long-term view.

ON Semiconductor restructured its Synaptics acquisition into an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $5.7 billion, reduced from the initial $7 billion stock-based proposal.
Synaptics shareholders will receive $123 cash per share rather than the previously agreed 1.350 ON shares from the June announcement.
ON stock surged approximately 6% during premarket hours, while Synaptics shares climbed roughly 14%.
The restructured agreement eliminates shareholder dilution concerns for ON investors and promises immediate accretion to non-GAAP earnings.
Completion of the transaction requires Synaptics shareholder approval and regulatory clearances, with an expected closing date in mid-2027.
Shares of ON Semiconductor rallied approximately 6% in Friday’s premarket session following the company’s announcement of a restructured takeover agreement with Synaptics. The stock had ended Thursday’s session at $80.08.
Synaptics shares posted even stronger gains, climbing approximately 14% on the announcement. Both semiconductor companies specialize in chip technologies for automotive, industrial, and Internet of Things applications.
The initial agreement, announced in June, proposed an all-stock merger structure. Under those terms, Synaptics shareholders would have exchanged each share for 1.350 ON Semiconductor shares, establishing a transaction value near $7 billion.
The revised agreement converts the transaction to an all-cash purchase. Synaptics shareholders will now receive $123 in cash per share, reducing the total transaction value to approximately $5.7 billion.
The price reduction followed an unsolicited competing proposal for Synaptics from an unnamed third party. Rather than triggering a competitive bidding situation that elevated the acquisition price, the development prompted both parties to negotiate modified terms more favorable to each company.
ON shareholders sidestep the equity dilution that would have resulted from issuing new shares under the original agreement. This change eliminates a significant concern that had pressured the stock since the June announcement.
The company indicates the restructured transaction will immediately enhance its non-GAAP earnings per share. This represents a meaningful improvement from the original structure, which wasn’t projected to be immediately accretive to earnings.
ON had previously identified $200 million in annual cost synergies from the combination. The company now anticipates additional opportunities, including potential revenue synergies and internalizing certain Synaptics manufacturing operations.
The transaction will be funded through a combination of existing cash reserves and debt financing arranged by Morgan Stanley. The absence of a financing contingency for closing eliminates another potential risk factor.
Synaptics CEO Rahul Patel characterized the cash structure as delivering certainty to investors. “We are providing value certainty at a premium as compared to current value,” he said.
The revised terms present a clear tradeoff. Synaptics shareholders forfeit potential participation in the merged entity’s future performance, receiving instead a guaranteed cash payment.
Robert W. Baird analyst Tristan Gerra maintained a Hold rating on ON stock following the announcement, keeping his $108 price target. The broader Wall Street consensus rates ON a Moderate Buy, while Synaptics carries a Hold rating.
Market timing also worked in the company’s favor. Micron’s impressive earnings results released the previous evening had already elevated semiconductor stocks broadly, providing additional momentum for ON’s announcement heading into Friday’s opening.
Treasury yields retreated from recent peaks that same morning, relieving some pressure on growth-oriented technology stocks.
The acquisition still requires approval from Synaptics shareholders alongside regulatory clearances. While the FTC has already granted approval, reviews in additional jurisdictions remain pending.
The companies are targeting a mid-2027 closing timeline. Between now and then, both stocks will likely respond to progress updates on the approval process.

ON Semiconductor (NASDAQ:ON | ON Price Prediction) trades at $68.30 after a brutal summer, while the average Wall Street price target sits at $106.88. That leaves the stock roughly 56% below where analysts, on average, think it should trade.
ON is the Phoenix-based designer behind onsemi, a top supplier of intelligent power and sensing chips for cars, factories, and increasingly, AI server racks. Its EliteSiC silicon carbide and GaNEXUS gallium nitride families are pitched as the plumbing for 800-volt vehicle platforms and the next generation of hyperscaler power trees. Wall Street cares because that story sits at the intersection of two of the biggest capex cycles in tech.
Even after a brutal selloff, business metrics are improving and analysts have not wavered. One has doubled down.
A Three-Month Wipeout in a Rallying Market
Shares of ON have plunged 43.84% over the past three months, a decline steep enough to qualify as a full-blown crash. The stock started that window at $121.62 and has bled all the way down to its current level, with a 14% drop just in the last month.
The selloff came despite strong results. Q2 fiscal 2026 revenue of $1.60 billion beat estimates and rose 9.18% year over year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.74 topping the $0.7153 consensus. Shares popped more than 5% after the report. The unwind has been driven by broader concerns: high automotive exposure, China cyclicality, a rich trailing valuation, and profit-taking after a run that had ON near $134.92 on a 52-week basis. The peer group softened too, but ON fell harder and faster.
Why Susquehanna Still Sees Roughly 120% Upside
Analysts have not chased the stock lower. Coverage sits at 2 Strong Buy, 11 Buy, 16 Hold, and zero Sell ratings, and estimate revisions have skewed sharply higher, with 25 upward EPS revisions for fiscal 2026 in the trailing 30 days against just two down.
Susquehanna’s Christopher Rolland reiterated a Buy with a Street-high $150 price target, implying roughly 120% upside from $68.30. His thesis: EliteSiC capturing dominant share as EV platforms shift from 400V to 800V architectures, AI data center power scaling through smart power stages and point-of-load converters, and gross margins recovering toward 40%+.
Management backs that narrative. AI data center is now expected to more than double in 2026. CEO Hassane El-Khoury told investors, “Our growth in data center is literally from the wall to the core.” Silicon carbide revenue in data centers is guided to grow nearly 60% year over year, with content per rack jumping from $15,000 to $115,000 in an 800-volt DC architecture. Non-GAAP gross margin already expanded to 39.3%, with Q3 guidance calling for 40% to 42%.
Analog Peers Held Up While ON Broke Down
This selloff is largely a single-name story. Peers softened but held ground.
NXP Semiconductors (NASDAQ:NXPI) trades at $227.95 against a target of $311.10, roughly 36% of implied upside. NXPI is up 5.02% year to date with 6 Strong Buy, 16 Buy, 7 Hold and 1 Sell ratings, a solidly bullish tilt.

SCOTTSDALE, Ariz. and SAN JOSE, Calif. – Oct. 1, 2026 – onsemi (NASDAQ: ON) and Synaptics Incorporated (NASDAQ: SYNA) ("Synaptics") today announced they have amended
their June 25, 2026 merger agreement. The amendment follows an unsolicited competing proposal received from a third party.
Under the revised agreement, onsemi will acquire Synaptics for $123 per share in cash for an aggregate value of approximately $5.7 billion as compared to approximately $7
billion for the prior agreement. The transaction is expected to be immediately accretive to onsemi’s non-GAAP earnings per share and provides value certainty for Synaptics’ shareholders.
“As was the case when we initially announced the acquisition, Synaptics addresses an important aspect of our strategic direction, and we believe the revised merger
agreement represents a more financially attractive transaction for our shareholders,” said Hassane El-Khoury, President and CEO of onsemi. “The all-cash transaction delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration,
and we now expect the transaction to be immediately accretive to non-GAAP EPS upon closing. In addition, we have identified incremental opportunities to create shareholder value beyond the previously announced $200 million of annual run-rate
synergies. These additional benefits from revenue synergies and insourcing of a portion of Synaptics’ production are expected to be realized after the initial 18 months
post-close, further strengthening the long-term earnings and cash flow profile of the combined company.”
El-Khoury continued, “Synaptics is accretive to our long-term model, with a strong growth outlook and attractive gross margin profile that will help accelerate onsemi’s
evolution. Additionally, Synaptics complements growth in our AI data center business, and brings to onsemi its highly profitable human-machine interface, and sensing products businesses that generate strong and predictable cash flows, providing the
combined company with a durable funding engine to accelerate its connected compute capabilities.”
After careful review with its financial and legal advisors, the Synaptics Board unanimously determined that the onsemi transaction, as amended, continues to be in the
best interests of Synaptics and its shareholders.
"Our Board has been singularly focused on delivering the best outcome for our shareholders, and today's amended agreement reflects that commitment," said Rahul Patel,
Synaptics President and CEO. “By transitioning to an all-cash structure, we are providing value certainty at a meaningful premium as compared to current value. We are confident this path is the right choice for our shareholders."
The transaction will be financed through a combination of cash on hand and committed financing. onsemi has obtained fully committed debt financing from Morgan Stanley.
The amended merger agreement does not include a closing condition related to onsemi’s financing.
The transaction is still expected to close by mid-2027, subject to approval by Synaptics shareholders, the receipt of required regulatory approvals and other customary
closing conditions. The transaction has been approved by the United States Federal Trade Commission, and regulators in other jurisdictions are reviewing the transaction.
